newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic sees 25pct long distance share.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic sees 25pct long distance share.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp Chairman Raymond Smith said Friday that he aims to grab 25 percent market share of the long-distance market over the next five years.
"We think we will get about 25 percent market share over four to five years," Smith said at the company's shareholder meeting in Wilmington, Delaware.
Smith, also the company's chief executive, said he expected the new Bell Altantic to expand into long-distance service before the end of this year.
"We will get in somewhere for sure in 1997 and everywhere in 1998," he said.
Smith also said he expected the NYNEX Corp merger to close "definitely by the end of May and maybe before that."

NYNEX and Bell Atlantic agreed to merge last year, forming the largest local phone provider in the country. The deal, valued at about $20 billion, would create an entity that stretches from Maine to Virginia.
Smith said the new entity will see cost savings of about $1 billion a year.
"We will be able to save about $600 million in expenses and about $400 million to $500 million in capital," Smith said.

The U.S. Department of Justice approved the merger last week. The only necessary approval remaining is that of the Federal Communications Commission, which needs to approve the transfer of cellular licenses from NYNEX to Bell Atlantic.
Smith said he expected the merger to close immediately after the anticipated FCC approval.
